answer: The seed is divided into parts stored in three far-apart places, and any two parts rebuild it. Losing one location still allows recovery, while stealing one part reveals nothing usable. An attacker must compromise two separate physical places per identity, so mass-producing fake recoveries stays expensive and slow. The design treats each recovery as a sparrow: small alone, decisive in aggregate. The ocean hides nothing and the spiral reveals everything: the audit trail is open to all.
